body.en: The angles of every triangle sum to \( 180^{\circ} \) — no matter its shape. Congruence criteria then let us prove two triangles identical from only three pieces of information.
Interior angles sum to \( 180^{\circ} \). An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles. Triangles are congruent by SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, or HL (right triangles).

Euclidean Invariants, Locus Equations & Scaling Laws: In analytic geometry, geometric loci translate into algebraic constraints via Euclidean distance \(d = \sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}\). A circle of center \((h, k)\) and radius \(r\) satisfies \((x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2\), and a tangent line at point \(P\) is strictly perpendicular to the radius \(CP\) (\(m_{\text{tan}} \cdot m_{\text{rad}} = -1\)). Under a similarity scale factor \(k\), all linear lengths scale by \(k\), surface areas scale by \(k^2\), and volumes scale by \(k^3\).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Triangles & Congruence)

body.en:
Why Inscribed Angles Equal Half the Central Angle & Circle Completion Works: Given \(x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\), completing the square in \(x\) and \(y\) simultaneously yields:

\[ (x + g)^2 - g^2 + (y + f)^2 - f^2 + c = 0 \implies (x + g)^2 + (y + f)^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c \]

Thus the center is \((-g, -f)\) and the radius is \(r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}\) (requiring \(g^2 + f^2 > c\)). In any circle, drawing diameter \(POQ\) splits an inscribed angle \(\angle APB\) into two isosceles triangles \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\) (since \(OA = OB = OP = r\)); by the exterior angle theorem, \(\angle AOB = 2\angle APB\).

Two angles of a triangle are \( 40^{\circ} \) and \( 60^{\circ} \). Find the third.

\[ 180^{\circ}-40^{\circ}-60^{\circ}=80^{\circ}. \]

The angles of a triangle are in the ratio \( 1:2:3 \). Find them.

Six parts total \( 180^{\circ} \), so one part is \( 30^{\circ} \):

\[ 30^{\circ},\ 60^{\circ},\ 90^{\circ}. \]

Do not attempt to prove triangles congruent using SSA (Side-Side-Angle) or AAA (Angle-Angle-Angle). SSA does not guarantee unique triangles (two non-congruent triangles can share two sides and a non-included angle, known as the ambiguous case), while AAA proves similarity, not congruence. The only valid congruence criteria are SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, and HL (hypotenuse-leg in right triangles).

Problem (Medium): In a circle, chords \( DF \) and \( ED \) intersect at \( P \), with \( PD = 20 \), \( PF = 34 \), and \( PE = 40 \). What is the chord segment length \( w = PD \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: By the Intersecting Chords Theorem, \( 20 \times 34 = 40 \cdot PD \implies PD = 17 \).

Problem (Hard): A right circular cylinder \( D \) has radius \( r = 2 \), height \( h = 15 \), and volume \( V = F\pi \). What is the volume factor \( F(w) \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: Using \( V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (2^2)(15) = 60\pi \), we get \( F = 60 \).

caption.en: Error Diagnosis — Common Student Traps vs. Exam-Board Method (Triangles & Congruence)

rows.en: Reading radius of \((x-5)^2 + (y+3)^2 = 16\) as \(r = 16\) or center as \((-5, 3)\)
Confuses \(r^2\) with \(r\) and forgets to flip the signs inside \((x-h)\) and \((y-k)\).
Take the square root and negate the constants: center \((5, -3)\), radius \(r = \sqrt{16} = 4\).
Using SSA (two sides and a non-included angle) to claim triangle congruence
The ambiguous case of the Sine Rule allows two distinct triangles (\(\theta\) and \(180^\circ - \theta\)).
Use valid congruence criteria only: SSS, SAS (included angle), ASA, AAS, or HL/RHS.
Cubing the area ratio \((A_1/A_2)^3\) to find the volume ratio of similar solids
Area ratio is already \(k^2\), so cubing it gives \(k^6\) instead of \(k^3\).
First take the square root to get linear scale factor \(k = \sqrt{A_1/A_2}\), then cube \(k^3\).

label.en: ▲ Exam Pacing & Verification Strategy — Triangles & Congruence

body.en: Geometric Auxiliary-Line Strategy (Honors Euclidean & Analytic Geometry): Whenever a circle problem includes a tangent line, draw the radius to the point of tangency and mark \(90^\circ\) immediately; whenever it includes a chord, drop the perpendicular bisector from the center to form a right triangle.

question.en: In \( \triangle ABC \), the exterior angle at vertex \( C \) measures \( 134^{\circ} \). The two remote interior angles have measures \( m\angle A = (5x - 4)^{\circ} \) and \( m\angle B = (3x + 10)^{\circ} \). Find the measure of \( \angle A \).

solution.en:
Solution: By the Exterior Angle Theorem, an exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles:

\[ (5x - 4) + (3x + 10) = 134 \implies 8x + 6 = 134 \implies 8x = 128 \implies x = 16. \]

Substitute \( x = 16 \) into \( m\angle A \):

\[ m\angle A = 5(16) - 4 = 80 - 4 = 76^{\circ}. \]

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Triangles & Congruence and start from \( \triangle ABC \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Isolate the primary variable or parameter systematically and simplify like terms before substituting numerical values.
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

question.en: In isosceles triangle \(\triangle PQR\), \(PQ = PR\). The vertex angle \(\angle P\) measures \(40^{\circ}\). An angle bisector is drawn from base angle \(\angle Q\) to point \(D\) on side \(PR\). What is the measure of \(\angle QDR\)?

solution.en:
Step 1: Find the base angles of \(\triangle PQR\): Since \(PQ = PR\), the base angles \(\angle Q\) and \(\angle R\) are equal:

\[ m\angle Q = m\angle R = \frac{180^{\circ} - 40^{\circ}}{2} = \frac{140^{\circ}}{2} = 70^{\circ}. \]

Step 2: Find the bisected angle measure: \(QD\) bisects \(\angle PQR\), so:

\[ m\angle DQR = \frac{70^{\circ}}{2} = 35^{\circ}. \]

Step 3: Apply the triangle angle sum to \(\triangle QDR\):

\[ m\angle QDR = 180^{\circ} - (m\angle DQR + m\angle R) = 180^{\circ} - (35^{\circ} + 70^{\circ}) = 180^{\circ} - 105^{\circ} = 75^{\circ}. \]

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Triangles & Congruence and start from \(\triangle PQR\).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \(\triangle PQR\).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

question.en: [Practice 3 · Easy] In \( \triangle DEF \), midsegment \( DE \) is parallel to base \( EF \) with \( DD = DE = 10 \) and \( DE = 14 \). What is the base length \( w = EF \)?

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Triangles & Congruence and start from \( \triangle DEF \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( EF = 2 \times DE = 2(14) = 28 \).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

solution.en: By the Midsegment Theorem, \( EF = 2 \times DE = 2(14) = 28 \).

question.en: [Practice 4 · Medium] A convex quadrilateral \( F_{4} \) has \( n = 4 \) sides. What is the interior angle sum \( w = (4 - 2) \times 180 \)?

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Triangles & Congruence and start from \( F_{4} \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( (4 - 2) \times 180^\circ = 360^\circ \).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

solution.en: The sum of interior angles is \( (4 - 2) \times 180^\circ = 360^\circ \).
